findings.claim: No test asserts the inclusive grant boundary (current + requested == max_allowed), so a > to >= mutation survives
findings.failure_mechanism: boundary shifted to >= -> exact-fit request denied -> no test fails
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: quota.py:4 uses > for deny, and lead probe allocate('t1',5,5,10) grants 5 with 'ok'; the contract names no required test

findings.claim: Deny-path tests do not assert the full response shape or remaining, so an R3 violation on deny responses could survive
findings.failure_mechanism: extra/missing key added to a deny response -> shape test only exercises the ok path -> regression survives
findings.rejection_reason: test-strength on correct code: quota.py:3 and quota.py:5 return exactly {granted, reason, remaining}, confirmed by lead probes

findings.claim: The unauthorized response exposes the internal usage counter by returning remaining = current
findings.failure_mechanism: empty tenant_id -> response echoes current -> counter value disclosed
findings.rejection_reason: current is an argument the caller supplied; echoing it back to that caller is not exposure of internal state, and the contract names no less-trusted response recipient; remaining on deny is unspecified by the contract
